name: Harrison James Ltd (accountants)
seen: The logo is a gold outlined shield with an HJ monogram; in the footer it sits above HARRISON JAMES LTD in white on navy.
Pages are pale grey-blue and white, with a navy call-to-action band and footer. There is a moon icon in the header for a dark theme.
Every button that matters is mustard-gold with navy text; headlines are navy. Nothing else is used as an accent.
Headings are a heavy geometric sans; body text is a plain neutral sans.
Corners are modestly rounded; cards have thin borders; the four How we work steps sit in gold numbered circles.

The home page runs: centred headline and two buttons, three audience cards (growing businesses, freelancers, property investors), a grid of services, four steps, a navy call to action, a footer with the Brackley address. The first screen has no photo.
The About page opens with a wide photo of a crowded open-plan room of people at laptops, tinted navy. It looks like a large tech event and does not match a small practice.
Pricing shows three tiers: Starter from £150 a month, Growth from £400 (badged Most Popular), Partner from £800. The page calls them indicative.
The page called Case Studies says the practice is new and has nothing to show yet, with a button to book a call.
The Contact page has a form (including an annual turnover band) beside a details box with the company number.
check: Where the About-page photo came from, and whether it can stand for this practice, is not known.
Nothing on the site shows which package clients actually choose. The Most Popular badge needs evidence or should go.
The client's own words about customers, worries and reasons for choosing a practice are not on the site. That is what the job map needs.
The Contact page took long to load in the capture; the page did appear.
The cookie bar was left open at the bottom.

today.accent: Mustard-gold buttons on navy and grey-blue

today.shape: Modest corners, thin-bordered cards, gold number circles

method: Screenshots taken with scripts/visual/capture.mjs and looked at by eye. Descriptions say what was visible on the screen. Font names, hex codes and image ownership were not read from code and are not claimed.
